subject: Regional dedicated capacity request / sizing (US, EU, APAC)
messages:
From: Emma Liu <emma@cloudmetrics.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Feb 2024 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Dedicated capacity sizing request — US/EU/APAC

Hi Marissa,

Following up from last week's call — CloudMetrics is preparing a commitment that will require regionally isolated dedicated pools across US, EU, and APAC. We want to avoid a single cross-region pool: regulatory teams insist on regional isolation for EU customers and APAC pilots.

High-level load estimates (initial forecast for Q3 launch):
- US: steady 180–220 RPS (inference request/sec) peak, model mix: 60% small/medium completion models, 30% large 70B class for key workflows, 10% embeddings.
- EU: steady 60–90 RPS, heavier on embeddings and mid-sized completions.
- APAC: 40–70 RPS, will start in Singapore and expand later.

We attached a spreadsheet with session-level traffic and a PO stub. Please share:
1) Recommended GPU pool sizes per region (node count and GPU type) and assumptions (batching, latency SLOs, caching).
2) Expected lead time to provision Dedicated pools in each region.
3) Any recommended fallback policies (regional burst or cross-region failover) to keep SLAs during spikes.
4) Preliminary pricing ranges we can use for internal budgeting.

We'd like a one-page sizing proposal and an MPA outline by end of next week if possible.

Thanks—
Emma Liu
Head of AI Ops, CloudMetrics
emma@cloudmetrics.com

Attachments: CloudMetrics_Dedicated_Request_Q2.xlsx, PO_stub_CloudMetrics.pdf

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity sizing request — US/EU/APAC

Emma — thanks for the clear numbers and the PO stub. Looping in Avery and Connor to provide a sizing sketch and lead-time estimates; Vivek to align on commercial structure.

Our plan: Avery will draft a conservative GPU pool recommendation per region (including safety margin + burst config). Connor will confirm provisioning lead times and any infra constraints in the EU/SG regions. I'll consolidate into a one-page proposal and draft MPA redlines.

Quick questions to help sizing:
- Target p99 latency SLO for completion requests? (e.g., <200ms token latency or end-to-end <1.2s for short prompts)
- For large 70B model traffic, can you share % of calls that require full sequence generation (long-range) vs short completions?

If we can get those two datapoints today, we can accelerate the sizing doc.

Best,
Marissa Cole

From: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Emma Liu <emma@cloudmetrics.com>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Feb 2024 13:20:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity sizing request — US/EU/APAC

Emma / team — I ran quick throughput sims against the model mix you provided using our serving profiles. Assumptions: batch size 8 for small/medium models, 1–2 for 70B class with KV cache hotness ~45%. Average token generation per request assumed 64 tokens (short completions).

Preliminary sizing (conservative):
- US pool: 8 x A100-80GB GPUs (4 replicas, each replica 2 GPUs, optimized for 70B q4/ptq) — supports ~200 RPS with 20% headroom for bursts (estimated steady token throughput ~12k tokens/sec).
- EU pool: 3 x A100-80GB GPUs (single replica across 3 GPUs for redundancy) — supports ~75 RPS with batching tuned to region latency SLOs.
- APAC pool: 2 x A100-80GB GPUs (single replica) — supports ~60 RPS, recommended pilot config with autoscale to +1 GPU during predictable business hours.

Notes and tradeoffs:
- If a lot of large full-sequence generations (>256 tokens), increase GPU counts by ~25–40% per region or increase replicas.
- Using quantized model variants (q4_hybrid) reduces memory pressure and allows higher concurrent QPS; we should validate quality on your eval set.
- Recommend per-route caching for frequently repeated prompts and an LRU KV cache window to cut load ~12–18%.

I'll attach a region_capacity_map and the simple calculator I used. Happy to walk through the math on a call.

-Avery
Avery Johnson
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
avery_johnson@redwood.com

Attachments: region_capacity_map.png

From: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.com>, Emma Liu <emma@cloudmetrics.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 13 Feb 2024 08:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity sizing request — US/EU/APAC

Marissa / team — a few infra realities to call out: provisioning Dedicated pools in the US (us-west) is typically 2–3 weeks once a PO/commit is accepted (capacity permitting). EU (Frankfurt) takes 3–5 weeks currently due to rack availability and compliance checks for EU data residency. APAC (Singapore) lead time is often 4–6 weeks.

Operational recommendations:
- Add a 20% headroom buffer to Avery's numbers for the first 90 days; initial traffic tends to be burstier than forecasted.
- Enable regional burst policies: allow a small cross-region spillover for short durations (we preserve encryption-in-flight and only enable with customer opt-in). For CloudMetrics' EU regulatory case, we recommend a hard block on EU -> non-EU data copying but allow compute failover with sanitized payloads if required for availability.
- If procurement wants on-prem OEM GPU hardware, lead times jump to 10+ weeks and require an installation window.

I'll prepare a provisioning timeline matrix for each region and share expected SLO attainment per config.

Connor O'Brien
Head of Infrastructure, Redwood Inference
connor_obrien@redwood.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Date: Wed, 14 Feb 2024 11:10:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity sizing request — US/EU/APAC

Emma — consolidating Avery and Connor's inputs, attached is a one-page proposal and an MPA redline snapshot. High-level proposal:
- US pool (priority #1): 8x A100-80GB (prod-ready) — target provision in 2–3 weeks after PO.
- EU pool (priority #2): 4x A100-80GB (prod) — target 3–5 weeks; include EU-only data residency clause.
- APAC pool (pilot): 2x A100-80GB with autoscale to +1 GPU — target 4–6 weeks.

Commercials (ballpark for internal planning):
- Committed monthly spend approx: US $85k/mo, EU $40k/mo, APAC $22k/mo (includes support and a 15% operational buffer). Final pricing depends on exact replica topology and commitment term.

Next steps:
1) Confirm priority region (which pool we should provision first).
2) Sign PO for the initial commitment (we can stage region provisioning against the same PO).
3) Review MPA redlines — I've highlighted EU data residency and backup/restore clauses.

If this looks reasonable, we can draft a formal quote and a provisioning timeline matrix for legal/procurement.

Thanks and happy to review live on Friday.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Principal Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

Attachments: Draft_MPA_redlines_v1.pdf, CloudMetrics_Dedicated_Request_Q2.xlsx
